addressed.instructions: The anchor requires a stated reason for every cron command that does not go through the shared command path. Decide whether `item.text` meets it. It is met when the item states that every cron command goes through the shared path, or that no cron command is off, excluded from, or bypassing it (then no reason is needed), or when every cron command the item places outside the shared path has a reason in the text. Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.unclear: The item discusses cron commands and the shared path but it cannot be told whether any cron command is off the path or whether a reason is given.

contradicted.instructions: Is there a cron command that `item.text` says does not go through the shared command path and for which `item.text` gives no reason? Saying that reasons are not required also counts. Do not count commands the item says go through the shared path. Silence about cron routing does not count. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: Yes: at least one cron command is off the shared path with no reason given, or the item says no reason is needed.
criteria.no: No: no cron command is said to be off the shared path, or each off-path one has a reason, or the item does not discuss cron routing.
criteria.unclear: The item's wording leaves it undecidable whether some off-path cron command lacks a reason.

addressed.instructions: An item satisfies this anchor in one of two ways: (A) it says every cron command goes through the shared command path, so no command is off it and no reason is required; or (B) it names the cron commands that stay off the shared path and gives the reason for each. Does `item.text` do (A) or (B)? A general mention of cron and the shared path without saying which commands are off it does neither. Judge presence only.

criteria.yes: The item does (A) or (B).
criteria.no: The item does neither: it is silent about cron routing, only mentions the topic, or names an off-path cron command without its reason.
criteria.unclear: The item says something about cron routing but it cannot be told whether it does (A) or (B).

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` place a cron command outside the shared command path (it bypasses the path, keeps its own storage call, is handled outside it, or calls a backend directly) without giving a reason for that command, or state that off-path cron commands need no reason? An item that puts every cron command on the shared path is not a conflict. Silence about cron routing is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: Some cron command is stated to be off the shared path and no reason for it appears in the item, or the item says reasons are not needed.
criteria.no: Every cron command the item places off the shared path has a reason, or the item places none off it, or the item is silent about cron routing.
criteria.unclear: The item may place a cron command off the shared path without a reason, but the wording does not settle it.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` about cron commands or the shared command path? Count any item that adds or changes a cron command (cron.start, cron.end, cron.list or similar), edits sc-cron-commands, edits Transform/storage_read/storage_write, or says which cron commands go through the shared path. Judge relevance only.

criteria.yes: At least one of those kinds of work or statements is in the item.
criteria.no: None of those appear; the item is about unrelated work.
criteria.unclear: It is impossible to tell from the text whether any of those appear.

anchor.statement: The sprint text MUST state a reason for each cron command that does not go through the shared command path.
anchor.scope: plan items that change cron commands, sc-cron-commands or the shared command path
